items.title: The Balcony
items.description_narrative: Modeled in part on Goya's 'Majas on a Balcony,' the painting groups the painter Berthe Morisot, violinist Fanny Claus, and painter Antoine Guillemet on a green-shuttered balcony. Its flat, high-contrast forms and detached figures unsettled critics at the 1869 Salon.
items.tags: balcony, group portrait, Berthe Morisot, Salon, Paris, green shutters
items.credit_line: ggFK0UgXAd7OCA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Hare (Un Lièvre)
items.description_narrative: A dead hare hangs against a plain dark background in a still life indebted to the 18th-century game paintings of Chardin, a recurring reference point for Manet's early still-life work. The subject reflects a traditional French still-life genre that Manet returned to throughout his career.
items.tags: still life, game, hare, Chardin influence, dark background, early work

items.title: Vase of White Lilacs and Roses
items.description_narrative: Painted in the last months of Manet's life, this bouquet of white lilacs and pink roses is one of a series of small floral still lifes he made for friends who visited him during his final illness. The loose, vigorous brushwork belies the confinement in which it was painted.
items.tags: still life, lilacs, roses, late work, Dallas Museum of Art, floral bouquet

items.title: The Toilers of the Sea
items.description_narrative: Three fishermen strain at the oars of a small boat tossed on choppy water, their faces reduced to a few economical brushstrokes. Manet, an avid sailor in his youth, returned repeatedly across his career to scenes of the sea and coastal labor.
items.tags: seascape, fishermen, boat, marine painting, maritime labor, sketch-like brushwork
items.credit_line: gAH4SR-FUI_RBA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Interior at Arcachon
items.description_narrative: Manet painted this intimate domestic scene of his wife Suzanne and stepson Léon at a window in Arcachon shortly after rejoining his family following the Franco-Prussian War. Never exhibited in his lifetime, the loosely brushed picture has the quality of a private, personal record.
items.tags: interior, domestic scene, family portrait, seaside, Arcachon, Suzanne Manet

items.title: Music in the Tuileries Gardens
items.description_narrative: Manet gathered friends, family, and fellow artists — including Baudelaire and Offenbach — into a crowded, fashionable scene of open-air concertgoers in the Tuileries Gardens. Its sketch-like handling and depiction of contemporary leisure make it a founding work of modern-life painting.
items.tags: Tuileries Gardens, Paris, crowd scene, modern life, leisure, group portrait

items.title: Vase of Flowers, Roses and Lilac
items.description_narrative: One of roughly sixteen small floral still lifes Manet painted in the last year of his life, this bouquet of roses and lilac is distinguished by fallen green leaves scattered across the marble tabletop below. He worked on these pictures at an easel set up beside his sickbed as illness curtailed his mobility.
items.tags: still life, flowers, lilac, roses, late work, floral series

items.title: At the Café
items.description_narrative: Set in a Parisian café, the painting captures an assortment of patrons — a woman at a marble table, a man smoking, a waitress passing by — cropped as if glimpsed in passing. It exemplifies Manet's interest in the fleeting, fragmentary character of urban social life.
items.tags: café scene, Paris, modern life, genre painting, urban leisure, cropped composition
items.credit_line: GgEZL0iu5Gl9FA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Portrait of Antonin Proust
items.description_narrative: Manet portrayed his childhood friend and future Minister of Fine Arts, Antonin Proust, dressed elegantly in a coat, gloves, and top hat, and carrying a walking stick. The confident, informal pose reflects the close personal bond between the two men.
items.tags: portrait, Antonin Proust, friendship, Paris, top hat, formal dress
items.credit_line: ggF7lBxcneTLcw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Madame Manet in the Conservatory
items.description_narrative: Manet painted his wife Suzanne seated in the same glass conservatory that served as the setting for 'In the Conservatory,' where she often helped him by posing for other sittings. Intended as a private gift rather than a work for sale, it was sold by Suzanne only after the artist's death.
items.tags: conservatory, Suzanne Manet, portrait, private gift, greenery, Oslo
items.credit_line: Manet, Madame Manet in the Conservatory, 1879, National Gallery, Oslo (1)

items.title: Boats at Berck-sur-Mer
items.description_narrative: Painted during a stay near Boulogne, this small seascape captures sailboats dancing on blue-green waves under a rapidly brushed sky. Manet spent childhood summers by the sea and returned often to marine subjects throughout his career.
items.tags: seascape, sailboats, Berck-sur-Mer, marine painting, coastal scene, small format

items.title: View of the 1867 Exposition Universelle
items.description_narrative: From a private pavilion he built on high ground overlooking the Champ de Mars, Manet painted the sprawling grounds of the 1867 World's Fair, populated with scattered strolling figures rather than any focal event. He left the work unfinished, abandoning it to begin his paintings of Maximilian's execution.
items.tags: Paris, World's Fair, cityscape, modern life, unfinished, panoramic view
items.credit_line: Manet, View of the 1867 Exposition Universelle, 1867, National Gallery, Oslo (1)

items.title: The Ship's Deck
items.description_narrative: An early work in Manet's career-long fascination with the sea, this close-up view of a ship's deck, masts, and rigging is framed as though seen by a passenger or sailor standing at the rail. Unlike his later marine paintings, the sea itself is only glimpsed at the edges of the canvas.
items.tags: marine painting, ship, rigging, early work, sea voyage, seascape
items.credit_line: LQHyaioK9DJyQg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Women at the Races
items.description_narrative: Two fashionably dressed women, shaded by parasols, are shown as spectators at the horse races in the Bois de Boulogne. The picture is a surviving fragment of a larger 1864 composition of the Longchamp racecourse, from which the racing action itself was later removed.
items.tags: horse racing, Bois de Boulogne, fashion, modern life, fragment, spectators
items.credit_line: 5gFzqmCBV6HdXw at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Jesus Mocked by the Soldiers
items.description_narrative: One of Manet's rare religious subjects, the painting shows Christ crowned with thorns and mocked by Roman soldiers, rendered with the same flat, stark lighting he brought to his contemporary scenes. Exhibited at the 1865 Salon alongside 'Olympia,' it drew similarly harsh criticism for its unconventional handling of a traditional subject.
items.tags: religious painting, Christ, Salon, Chicago, history painting, 1865
items.credit_line: TwFXxhuKbiTsSg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Absinthe Drinker
items.description_narrative: One of Manet's earliest exhibited paintings, it portrays a shabbily dressed Parisian ragpicker beside a glass of absinthe, rendered with the dark tonality of Spanish old masters he admired. Rejected by the 1859 Salon jury, it nonetheless anticipated his later interest in marginal figures of modern city life.
items.tags: early work, Paris, absinthe, Salon rejection, Spanish influence, genre painting
items.credit_line: zwG8nxV1nz8icQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Basket of Fruit
items.description_narrative: A woven basket brimming with peaches, plums, and figs is rendered in the confident, wet-in-wet brushwork typical of Manet's still lifes from the mid-1860s. The painting reflects his lifelong admiration for the French still-life tradition of Chardin.
items.tags: still life, fruit, basket, Boston, Chardin influence, 1864
items.credit_line: 7wEOLcnwTUJzJw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Laundry (Le Linge)
items.description_narrative: Painted in the garden of his rented house in Paris, the picture shows a woman hanging washing while a young child looks on, one of Manet's few forays into a subject associated with his Impressionist peers. The dappled outdoor light and everyday domestic labor mark a departure from his usual urban subjects.
items.tags: garden, laundry, domestic labor, outdoor light, Barnes Foundation, everyday life

items.title: Bunch of Peonies
items.description_narrative: A loosely painted bouquet of peonies in full bloom fills the canvas, part of Manet's recurring practice of painting his favorite flower, which he also grew in his garden at Gennevilliers. Works like this belong to the free, economical late still lifes he produced increasingly as illness limited his output.
items.tags: still life, peonies, flowers, late work, Gennevilliers, floral bouquet

items.title: The Battle of the U.S.S. Kearsarge and the C.S.S. Alabama
items.description_narrative: Manet depicted the dramatic 1864 naval battle off Cherbourg between the Union warship Kearsarge and the Confederate raider Alabama, an event he may have witnessed from shore. The high horizon and turbulent water reflect his enduring interest in marine subjects and contemporary current events.
items.tags: naval battle, American Civil War, seascape, Cherbourg, history painting, Philadelphia
items.credit_line: TwEfQaofrflr0Q at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Gypsy with a Cigarette
items.description_narrative: A woman rests her head on her hand, a cigarette dangling from her lips, in a half-length composition once owned by Edgar Degas. Never exhibited or titled by Manet himself, the picture's subject and the title given it by later scholars reflect 19th-century exoticizing conventions surrounding Roma identity.
items.tags: portrait, Princeton, Degas provenance, smoking, half-length figure, 1862
items.credit_line: This image has been extracted from another file

items.title: La Parisienne (A Parisian Lady)
items.description_narrative: The actress Ellen Andrée is shown in profile, dressed entirely in fashionable black with a veil and gloves, epitomizing the stylish Parisian woman of the 1870s. The painting is held by the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm.
items.tags: portrait, fashion, Ellen Andrée, Paris, black dress, Stockholm

items.title: Boy in Flowers (Jacques Hoschedé)
items.description_narrative: Manet portrayed the young son of his patron and friend Ernest Hoschedé standing amid a bed of flowers, rendered with rapid, high-keyed brushwork. The painting reflects Manet's ties to the Hoschedé family, prominent collectors of Impressionist painting.
items.tags: child portrait, Jacques Hoschedé, flowers, patron, garden, Tokyo
items.credit_line: fAE1Q1sfj23yIQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Corner of a Café-Concert
items.description_narrative: A waitress carrying beer mugs pauses amid a crowd of smoking, drinking patrons at a Parisian café-concert, a popular venue mixing dining, drinking, and live entertainment. The painting was cut from a larger canvas that Manet divided in two, the other half now known as 'The Waitress.'
items.tags: café-concert, Paris, waitress, nightlife, modern life, cropped composition

items.title: Argenteuil
items.description_narrative: Painted during a stay with Monet at Argenteuil on the Seine, the picture shows a boater and a fashionably dressed woman seated by the riverbank, its brilliant blue water reflecting Manet's brief engagement with Impressionist plein-air technique. It was poorly received at the 1875 Salon for its bold, saturated color.
items.tags: Argenteuil, Seine, boating, Impressionism, Salon, riverside

items.title: Flowers in a Crystal Vase
items.description_narrative: A small, tightly cropped arrangement of flowers in a faceted crystal vase, painted with the rapid, abbreviated brushwork of Manet's final years. It belongs to the group of small floral still lifes he made as his health declined.
items.tags: still life, flowers, crystal vase, late work, Washington, floral bouquet
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: Oysters
items.description_narrative: A plate of freshly opened oysters, a lemon, and a knife are rendered with crisp, confident brushwork typical of Manet's early still-life painting. Still life subjects like this one allowed Manet to display his technical virtuosity outside the pressures of Salon-scale figure painting.
items.tags: still life, oysters, food, early work, National Gallery of Art, 1862
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: Still Life with Melon and Peaches
items.description_narrative: Ripe peaches and a sliced melon are arranged on a table alongside a knife and glass, painted with the direct, tactile brushwork Manet brought to still life throughout the 1860s. The work reflects his enduring debt to French still-life painters of the 18th century such as Chardin.
items.tags: still life, fruit, melon, peaches, Chardin influence, National Gallery of Art
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: The Melon
items.description_narrative: A single sliced melon rests on a table in one of the small, economically painted still lifes Manet produced late in his career, often as gifts to friends. Its spare composition and rapid brushwork are characteristic of his final decade.
items.tags: still life, melon, late work, small format, National Gallery of Art, gift painting
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: Peonies
items.description_narrative: A loose arrangement of pink and white peonies, Manet's favorite flower, fills this canvas from his mid-1860s series of peony still lifes. He returned to the subject repeatedly, producing roughly eight peony paintings across 1864 and 1865.
items.tags: still life, peonies, flowers, Metropolitan Museum, 1864, floral series
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art. See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy

items.title: The Brioche
items.description_narrative: A brioche loaf topped with a rose sits among fruit and a knife, a still life that consciously echoes 18th-century French tradition while also nodding to Chardin's own brioche compositions. It was painted the same year as several of Manet's most accomplished still lifes.
items.tags: still life, brioche, food, Chardin homage, Metropolitan Museum, 1870
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art. See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy

items.title: Peonies in a Bottle
items.description_narrative: Cut peony stems are gathered loosely in a plain glass bottle in this still life from Manet's mid-1860s series devoted to his favorite flower. Its informal vessel and pared-down composition contrast with the more decorative vases used in some of his other peony paintings.
items.tags: still life, peonies, flowers, bottle, 1864, floral series

items.title: Tarring the Boat (Le Bateau goudronné)
items.description_narrative: Painted during a summer stay on the Normandy coast, the picture shows fishermen at work tarring the hull of a beached boat, rendered with the loose, sketch-like brushwork of Manet's outdoor scenes of the early 1870s. It reflects his ongoing engagement with scenes of coastal labor.
items.tags: coastal labor, fishermen, boat, Normandy, Barnes Foundation, 1873

items.title: Woman Viewed from Behind (Visit to a Museum)
items.description_narrative: A woman in modern dress is seen from behind, gazing at unseen paintings in a gallery. The cropped, off-center view reflects Degas's fascination with unconventional vantage points borrowed from photography and Japanese prints.
items.tags: pastel, museum-goer, back view, modern life, Impressionism, Paris
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: Waiting (L'Attente)
items.description_narrative: A ballet dancer rubs her ankle while seated beside an older woman on a bench, likely her mother or chaperone waiting during a rehearsal break. The pastel captures a quiet, unposed backstage moment typical of Degas's ballet series.
items.tags: ballet, dancer, pastel, backstage, waiting, chaperone
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture: Home page – Image

items.title: Alexander and Bucephalus
items.description_narrative: An early history painting by the young Degas depicting Alexander the Great taming the wild horse Bucephalus. It reflects his academic training and admiration for classical and Renaissance subject matter before he turned to modern-life themes.
items.tags: history painting, Alexander the Great, horse, early work, academic, mythology
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: Mary Cassatt
items.description_narrative: A portrait of the American Impressionist painter Mary Cassatt, Degas's close friend and fellow exhibitor with the Impressionist group. She is shown seated informally, holding photographs, rather than in a conventional formal pose.
items.tags: portrait, Mary Cassatt, Impressionism, friendship, seated figure
items.credit_line: NQEN6L1Ys9hFvA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Russian Dancer
items.description_narrative: Part of Degas's late series of folk dancers in colorful peasant costume, painted from memory in his failing eyesight using bold, loosely worked pastel. The vivid color and simplified forms anticipate early modernist expressionism.
items.tags: dancer, pastel, folk costume, late work, color, movement
items.credit_line: VQEf_9v-hapiwg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Estérel Village
items.description_narrative: A landscape from Degas's series of imaginative pastel-over-monotype views inspired by the Estérel massif near Cannes, made after a carriage trip through the region. The atmospheric, semi-abstract handling shows Degas experimenting with landscape late in his career.
items.tags: landscape, Estérel, monotype, pastel, Cleveland Museum, late work

items.title: Laundresses (Wash Women)
items.description_narrative: Working-class laundresses are shown at their labor, a theme Degas returned to often as part of his broader interest in depicting ordinary working women of modern Paris. The composition emphasizes physical strain and unglamorized realism.
items.tags: laundresses, working women, modern life, genre scene, Dallas Museum

items.title: Young Woman Seated in an Armchair
items.description_narrative: A young woman is shown seated informally in an armchair, rendered in the broad, vigorous pastel strokes typical of Degas's late style as his eyesight failed. Its French title translates as 'Young Woman Seated in an Armchair.'
items.tags: pastel, seated woman, late work, informal portrait, armchair

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.medium: Oil on paper mounted on canvas
items.description_narrative: One of several self-portraits Degas made as a young man in his early twenties, before he had developed the modern-life subjects for which he later became known. It shows the influence of his academic training and admiration for Ingres.
items.tags: self-portrait, early work, Clark Art Institute, Realism, youth

items.title: Ludovic Lepic Holding His Dog
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Degas's friend, the painter and etcher Ludovic-Napoléon Lepic, shown informally with a dog. Lepic was part of Degas's circle of avant-garde artists in the early years of the Impressionist movement.
items.tags: portrait, Ludovic Lepic, dog, friendship, Cleveland Museum

items.title: Portrait of a Man
items.description_narrative: An unidentified male sitter is rendered with the restrained, dark-toned palette Degas favored in his early portrait work. The painting reflects his grounding in academic portraiture before his mature Impressionist style emerged.
items.tags: portrait, unidentified sitter, early work, Clark Art Institute, Realism

items.title: Two Horses Facing Left
items.description_narrative: A study of two horses in profile, facing left, related to Degas's lifelong preoccupation with the racetrack and equestrian subjects. Such studies fed into his finished racecourse paintings.
items.tags: horses, drawing, study, racetrack, sketch

items.title: Woman Drying Herself (1888–1892)
items.description_narrative: A nude woman is caught in the private act of drying herself after bathing, part of Degas's extensive late series of bather studies. He treated the subject almost obsessively, exploring the body in unguarded, everyday poses.
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, toilette, private moment

items.title: Young Woman in Blue
items.description_narrative: A partially unfinished portrait study of a young woman in a blue dress, showing Degas's underlying construction of a composition. Unfinished works like this one reveal his working method more directly than his completed portraits.
items.tags: portrait, unfinished, blue dress, young woman, working method
items.credit_line: LwH3Qmd571a-Jw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: After the Bath, Woman Drying Herself (1884–1886)
items.description_narrative: Another entry in Degas's series of bathers, showing a nude woman drying herself in an intimate interior. Held at the Musée d'art moderne André Malraux in Le Havre, it demonstrates the variety of poses he explored within a single recurring theme.
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, toilette, Le Havre

items.title: Woman Drying Herself
items.description_narrative: A late pastel bather study, its square format and broad handling typical of Degas's mature bathing-scene compositions. The figure's contorted pose reflects his interest in the body's mechanics rather than idealized beauty.
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, toilette, late work
items.credit_line: cgGZJZP5DWJbdg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Nude Woman Seated on the Ground, Combing Her Hair
items.description_narrative: A nude woman sits on the floor combing her hair, one of many hair-combing studies Degas produced in the 1880s at the Musée d'Orsay. The low, informal vantage point is characteristic of his bather compositions.
items.tags: bather, nude, hair-combing, pastel, Musée d'Orsay

items.title: At the Races in the Countryside
items.description_narrative: A carriage carrying Degas's friends the Valpinçon family and their infant, with a wet-nurse, pauses at a rural racecourse. It combines his interests in horse racing, portraiture, and modern bourgeois family life in a single scene.
items.tags: racecourse, carriage, family, Valpinçon, countryside, modern life
items.credit_line: fAG5E-YLY4Q57g at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Portrait of a Man (Diego Martelli), study
items.description_narrative: A study related to Degas's portraits of the Italian art critic Diego Martelli, an early champion of the Impressionists in Italy. Degas painted Martelli more than once around 1879, exploring different poses and settings.
items.tags: portrait, Diego Martelli, art critic, study, Clark Art Institute

items.title: Head of a Man
items.description_narrative: A close study of a man's head, part of Degas's continual practice of figure and portrait drawing outside his major finished works. Held at the National Museum in Belgrade, it shows his sustained interest in draftsmanship.
items.tags: portrait study, drawing, head, National Museum Belgrade

items.title: Horseman Seen from Behind, with Spurs
items.description_narrative: An early equestrian study showing a rider from behind, with close attention to the spurs and tack. It belongs to Degas's youthful preparatory studies for his history and racecourse paintings of the 1860s.
items.tags: horseman, equestrian, drawing, early work, study

items.title: Diego Martelli
items.description_narrative: A portrait of the Italian art critic and journalist Diego Martelli, one of the earliest Italian supporters of the Impressionists. Degas made related versions of this portrait around 1879, of which this is one.
items.tags: portrait, Diego Martelli, art critic, Cleveland Museum

items.title: After the Bath: Woman Drying Herself
items.description_narrative: A nude woman dries herself beside a tub in a warmly colored interior, part of Degas's long-running bather series now at the National Gallery, London. The pastel's rich orange and blue tones are characteristic of his late palette.
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, toilette, National Gallery London

items.title: Beach Scene
items.medium: Oil on paper mounted on canvas
items.description_narrative: A young girl has her hair combed on a beach while other figures rest nearby, painted using paper cut-outs arranged and reworked in the studio rather than outdoors. It shows Degas's unconventional, studio-based approach to a seemingly plein-air subject.
items.tags: beach, seaside, hair-combing, oil sketch, leisure
items.credit_line: 1. The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN: 3936122202. 2. The National Gallery

items.title: Promenade Beside the Sea
items.description_narrative: An early figure composition showing women walking along a shoreline, made before Degas turned decisively toward Parisian modern-life subjects. It reflects his youthful engagement with landscape and outdoor figure grouping.
items.tags: seaside, promenade, early work, figures, landscape

items.title: Ukrainian Dancers
items.description_narrative: A companion piece within Degas's late series of dancers in colorful Eastern European folk dress, worked in bold, expressive pastel strokes. The vividness of color anticipates the concerns of early 20th-century modernism.
items.tags: dancer, folk costume, pastel, late work, color

items.title: Combing the Hair (La Coiffure)
items.description_narrative: A striking, almost monochrome composition dominated by deep red, showing a maid combing the hair of a seated woman. Its flattened, decorative color scheme is among Degas's boldest experiments with Impressionist color.
items.tags: hair-combing, red, domestic scene, National Gallery, color experiment
items.credit_line: 1. The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN: 3936122202. 2. National Gallery, London - online collection

items.title: Paul Lafond and Alphonse Cherfils Examining a Painting
items.description_narrative: Two of Degas's friends, the museum curator Paul Lafond and the collector Alphonse Cherfils, are shown examining a painting together. The scene reflects Degas's own social world of collectors, critics, and fellow connoisseurs.
items.tags: portrait, Paul Lafond, art collecting, Cleveland Museum, friendship

items.title: Study for a Portrait of Hélène Rouart
items.description_narrative: A preparatory study for Degas's portrait of Hélène Rouart, daughter of his close friend and collector Henri Rouart. Degas made numerous studies of the sitter's pose and setting before completing the final oil portrait.
items.tags: portrait study, Hélène Rouart, drawing, preparatory work

items.title: Madame Jeantaud in the Mirror
items.description_narrative: A fashionable Parisian woman is shown before a mirror, her reflection cropped so that the viewer sees more of her reflected image than her actual face. The composition plays with mirrored space in a way Degas returned to often.
items.tags: portrait, mirror, Parisian fashion, reflection, modern life
items.credit_line: BgFg1OUqjIILuA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Visit to a Museum
items.description_narrative: Two women, one seated and one standing, look at paintings in a museum gallery, likely the Louvre. Related to Degas's pastel study 'Woman Viewed from Behind,' this finished oil version worked and reworked over a decade shows his interest in the act of looking at art.
items.tags: museum, gallery, modern life, oil painting, viewing art
items.credit_line: uQEaGdRyVjwCfg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Interior (The Rape)
items.description_narrative: A tense, narrative scene in a lamplit bedroom shows a man standing near a door while a partly undressed woman sits with her back to him. The ambiguous psychological drama, unusual for Degas, has long invited literary interpretations, including a possible source in Émile Zola.
items.tags: narrative scene, psychological tension, interior, bedroom, Realism
items.credit_line: wwFhoXRQJtHYJg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Billiard Room at Ménil-Hubert
items.description_narrative: An empty billiard room at Ménil-Hubert, the country estate of Degas's childhood friend Paul Valpinçon, painted during one of his visits there. The unpeopled, geometric interior is a rare example of pure interior/still-life subject matter in his work.
items.tags: interior, billiard room, Ménil-Hubert, Valpinçon, still life
items.credit_line: JAG3ooF4xPp0tg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: In a Café (L'Absinthe)
items.description_narrative: A man and a woman sit despondently at a Parisian café table, an absinthe glass before her, in one of Degas's most famous depictions of urban alienation. The models were his friends, the actress Ellen Andrée and the artist Marcellin Desboutin.
items.tags: café, absinthe, modern life, alienation, Musée d'Orsay, genre scene
items.credit_line: GQH1c-43xR3JtA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Portrait of the Art Critic Durand-Gréville
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Émile Durand-Gréville, a French art critic and writer contemporary with Degas. The work is held in the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm.
items.tags: portrait, art critic, Durand-Gréville, Nationalmuseum Stockholm

items.title: The Star (L'Étoile)
items.description_narrative: A solo ballerina takes a bow center stage, bathed in light, while shadowy figures — including a man in evening dress — linger in the wings behind her. One of Degas's most celebrated ballet pastels, held at the Musée d'Orsay.
items.tags: ballet, dancer, pastel, stage, Musée d'Orsay, iconic

items.title: Bedtime (Le Coucher)
items.description_narrative: An intimate scene of a woman preparing for bed, part of Degas's ongoing exploration of women's private domestic rituals. It is held at the National Museum of Serbia in Belgrade.
items.tags: domestic scene, bedtime, pastel, intimacy, National Museum Serbia

items.title: Toilette After the Bath
items.description_narrative: A woman attends to her hair or toilette after bathing, rendered in the dense, richly colored pastel technique of Degas's later years. The theme of a woman absorbed in private grooming recurs throughout his late bather series.
items.tags: bather, toilette, pastel, late work, private moment
items.credit_line: fQEGqK2IxtPRoQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Woman at Her Dressing Table
items.description_narrative: A woman is seated at her dressing table, part of Degas's recurring interest in women's private toilette rituals. Held at the Fondation Bemberg in Toulouse, it dates from 1879, during his most active pastel period.
items.tags: toilette, dressing table, pastel, Fondation Bemberg, domestic scene

items.title: After the Bath
items.description_narrative: A nude bather is shown in the aftermath of washing, part of the large series Degas exhibited at the eighth Impressionist exhibition of 1886. This version is held in Rome's Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna.
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, 1886 exhibition, Rome

items.title: Monsieur and Madame Édouard Manet
items.description_narrative: A double portrait of fellow painter Édouard Manet reclining while his wife Suzanne plays the piano. Manet reportedly slashed away the section depicting his wife's face, unhappy with Degas's rendering, leaving the canvas famously mutilated.
items.tags: portrait, Édouard Manet, double portrait, damaged canvas, friendship

items.title: Lorenzo Pagans and Auguste De Gas
items.description_narrative: The Spanish tenor Lorenzo Pagans sings while accompanied at the piano by Degas's own father, Auguste De Gas. The painting reflects the important role music played in the Degas family's social life.
items.tags: portrait, music, father, Lorenzo Pagans, Auguste De Gas

items.title: At the Milliner's
items.description_narrative: A customer tries on a hat while a milliner attends her, part of Degas's series of works depicting the millinery trade of Parisian hat shops. These scenes let him study fashion, labor, and social interaction between women.
items.tags: milliner, hat shop, pastel, fashion, Parisian trade

items.title: Breakfast After the Bath
items.description_narrative: A maid serves a nude woman a cup after her bath, combining Degas's bather theme with an added narrative element of domestic service. The title translates from the French as 'Breakfast After the Bath.'
items.tags: bather, domestic scene, maid, pastel, toilette

items.title: Seascape with Sandy Beach at Low Tide
items.description_narrative: A wide, nearly abstract view of a sandy beach exposed at low tide, part of a small group of pure landscape pastels Degas made along the Normandy coast. The German title translates as 'Seascape with Sandy Beach at Low Tide.'
items.tags: seascape, landscape, low tide, pastel, Normandy coast

items.title: Dancer Adjusting Her Shoe
items.description_narrative: A ballet dancer bends to fasten her shoe, a candid backstage gesture Degas depicted repeatedly across drawings, pastels, and sculpture. The French title translates as 'Dancer Fastening Her Shoe.'
items.tags: dancer, backstage, shoe, drawing, pastel, ballet

items.title: The Convalescent
items.description_narrative: A pale, seated woman wrapped in a shawl suggests recovery from illness, likely painted during Degas's travels to visit family in New Orleans. Its subdued palette and quiet mood are unusual within his broader body of work.
items.tags: portrait, illness, convalescence, New Orleans, seated figure
items.credit_line: EwEjiva1WNU2RQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Woman at Her Toilette (In Front of the Mirror)
items.description_narrative: A woman is shown at her toilette before a mirror, part of Degas's sustained investigation of women's private grooming rituals in the 1880s. The German title translates as 'In Front of the Mirror.'
items.tags: toilette, mirror, pastel, domestic scene, 1889

items.title: Woman Drying Her Left Leg
items.description_narrative: A nude bather bends to dry her leg, another variation within Degas's extensive bather series of the 1880s and 1890s. The Portuguese title translates as 'Woman Drying Her Left Leg.'
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, toilette, leg

items.title: Dancers in the Wings
items.description_narrative: Ballet dancers wait in the shadowy wings offstage, a recurring backstage vantage point Degas favored over the polished spectacle of performance itself. Held at the Norton Simon Museum.
items.tags: ballet, dancers, backstage, wings, pastel, Norton Simon
items.credit_line: 6wGQVgtOKBH9BA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Milliners
items.description_narrative: Two milliners are shown at work trimming hats in a shop interior, part of Degas's series documenting the trade. Now at the J. Paul Getty Museum, it captures the concentrated labor of the hatmaking craft.
items.tags: milliner, hat shop, labor, pastel, Getty Museum
items.credit_line: qgEZ0WlVeRlyFA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Woman Bathing
items.description_narrative: A nude woman is shown in the tub itself, rather than before or after bathing, a less common vantage within Degas's bather series. The Spanish title translates as 'Woman Bathing.'
items.tags: bather, nude, bathtub, pastel, toilette

items.title: Bathers
items.description_narrative: A grouping of nude bathers is depicted at their toilette, part of the Barnes Foundation's substantial holdings of Degas's late pastel work. The Barnes collection is especially rich in his bather and dancer subjects.
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, Barnes Foundation, group scene

items.title: Woman Drying Herself (1884)
items.description_narrative: A nude woman dries herself with a towel, one of Degas's earlier bather pastels dating to 1884, just before the theme became a dominant preoccupation in his later career.
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, toilette, 1884

items.title: Sulking (Bouderie)
items.description_narrative: A man and woman occupy the same office interior in evident tension, their averted postures suggesting an unspoken quarrel. The ambiguous narrative and modern office setting are characteristic of Degas's Realist genre scenes of the late 1860s and 1870s.
items.tags: narrative scene, office interior, tension, Realism, genre scene

items.title: Women Combing Their Hair
items.description_narrative: Several women are shown grooming and combing their hair together in an interior, an early treatment of a domestic ritual Degas would return to repeatedly in later pastels. Executed in oil, unusually, on paper.
items.tags: hair-combing, women, domestic scene, oil on paper, toilette
items.credit_line: vgHKz6OV4wcdug at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Seated Violin Player
items.description_narrative: A study of an orchestra musician seated with his violin, related to Degas's series of works depicting musicians and the Paris Opéra orchestra pit. Music-making was, alongside ballet, one of his recurring performance subjects.
items.tags: musician, violin, orchestra, Paris Opéra, study
items.credit_line: VwGyl7msPLDgaA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: After the Bath: Seated Woman Drying Herself
items.description_narrative: A nude woman sits drying herself, another variant within Degas's late bather series, worked in the dense, saturated color typical of his final decade of pastel production.
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, seated, toilette, late work
items.credit_line: NwF5Ztb_H-BT0g at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Village Street, Saint-Valery-sur-Somme
items.description_narrative: A quiet street view of the coastal town of Saint-Valery-sur-Somme in northern France, one of Degas's rare late landscape subjects. Held at the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek in Copenhagen.
items.tags: landscape, village, Saint-Valery-sur-Somme, Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
items.credit_line: Degas, Village Street, Saint-Valery-sur-Somme, 1896-98, Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek, Copenhagen by Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

items.title: Horses in a Meadow
items.description_narrative: Horses graze freely in an open meadow, one of Degas's smaller, more informal equestrian studies made outside the pressure of a racecourse composition. Held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: horses, meadow, landscape, oil on panel, National Gallery of Art
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: The Riders
items.description_narrative: Jockeys and riders are shown mounted, likely awaiting the start of a race, part of Degas's long fascination with the modern racetrack as a subject for studying movement. The scene favors preparation over the spectacle of the race itself.
items.tags: jockeys, horses, racecourse, riders, movement

items.title: Two Women
items.description_narrative: Two women are shown together in an informal interior, executed with Degas's pastel-over-monotype technique. Held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: women, interior, pastel, monotype, National Gallery of Art

items.title: Lady with a Dog

items.title: René De Gas

items.title: Young Woman with Her Hand over Her Mouth

items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, toilette, late work

items.title: Café-Concert
items.description_narrative: A singer performs at one of the popular open-air café-concerts of Paris, a form of entertainment Degas depicted repeatedly for its theatrical lighting and unconventional angles. Held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

items.title: Madame Dietz-Monnin
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Madame Dietz-Monnin, a Parisian society sitter, shown in an interior setting typical of Degas's independent portrait commissions of the late 1870s. Held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

items.description_narrative: A related study of the same sitter as Degas's National Gallery of Art oil portrait of Madame Dietz-Monnin, part of his practice of developing a composition across multiple sheets before a finished painting. Held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

items.title: Dancers at the Old Opera House
items.description_narrative: Dancers rehearse on the stage of the old Paris Opéra on the Rue Le Peletier, which burned down in 1873. Degas continued to paint this now-vanished theater from memory and earlier studies. Held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: ballet, dancers, Paris Opéra, rehearsal, National Gallery of Art

items.title: The Ballet Master (Le Maître de Ballet)
items.medium: Oil, essence, and pastel on paper
items.description_narrative: A ballet master oversees dancers rehearsing, a work Degas developed in part alongside his friend Vicomte Ludovic-Napoléon Lepic. Held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

items.title: Woman Drying Her Left Arm
items.description_narrative: A nude bather is shown drying her arm, one of the many closely related poses Degas explored within his late bather series. The Portuguese title translates as 'Woman Drying Her Left Arm.'
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, toilette, arm

items.title: Three Seated Women (Brothel Scene)
items.description_narrative: Three women sit together in a brothel interior, part of a series of small, frankly observed monotypes Degas made in the mid-1870s depicting life inside Parisian brothels. Held at the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: monotype, brothel scene, women, Rijksmuseum, Realism

items.title: Cotton Merchants in New Orleans
items.description_narrative: Merchants examine cotton samples in an office in New Orleans, painted during Degas's extended visit to his mother's American family, who were in the cotton trade. It relates to his more famous 'A Cotton Office in New Orleans.' Held at the Fogg Museum, Harvard University.
items.tags: cotton trade, New Orleans, commerce, family, Fogg Museum

items.title: Bather Drying Herself
items.description_narrative: A nude bather dries herself, another entry within Degas's extensive late series exploring the female nude at her toilette. The French title translates as 'Bather Drying Herself.'
items.tags: bather, nude, pastel, toilette, late work

items.title: Woman Drying Her Arm
items.description_narrative: A nude bather dries her arm after bathing, part of a set of related bather sheets held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, each capturing a different moment of the toilette ritual.

items.title: Male Nude (Academic Study)
items.description_narrative: An academic study of a standing male nude, from Degas's formal training period, likely made during his studies under Louis Lamothe or his time in Italy copying Renaissance masters.
items.tags: academic study, male nude, drawing, early work, training

items.title: Landscape
items.description_narrative: An imaginative, semi-abstract landscape made using Degas's pastel-over-monotype method, part of the series he produced following a carriage trip through Burgundy in the early 1890s. Held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: landscape, monotype, pastel, Metropolitan Museum, late work

items.title: Two Dancers, Half-Length
items.description_narrative: Two dancers are shown cropped at half-length, a close, informal framing Degas favored in his later ballet pastels. Held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

items.description_narrative: A bather bends to dry her foot, part of the same Metropolitan Museum group of closely related toilette studies as Degas's other 'Woman Drying' works.

items.description_narrative: A portrait believed to depict Degas's cousin Mathilde Musson, later Mrs. William Bell, painted during his visit to his mother's family in New Orleans. Held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

items.title: Woman Having Her Hair Combed
items.description_narrative: A maid combs the hair of a seated woman, part of Degas's series of hair-combing scenes exploring this everyday domestic ritual. Held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

items.title: Woman with a Towel
items.description_narrative: A nude woman holds a towel following her bath, another sheet in the Metropolitan Museum's series of closely related bather studies by Degas.

items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art. See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy

items.title: The Chemin de l'Écluse and the Pontoise Bridge
items.description_narrative: Pissarro painted this view of the lock path and bridge at Pontoise during the town's early years as his primary residence and subject, before the Franco-Prussian War interrupted his work there. The canvas belongs to his sustained study of the Oise riverbanks, rendered with the structured brushwork of his pre-Impressionist Pontoise period.
items.tags: Pontoise, Oise river, bridge, landscape, 1860s, riverside

items.title: Landscape near Pontoise, the Auvers Road
items.description_narrative: Painted along the road linking Pontoise to nearby Auvers-sur-Oise, this landscape dates from Pissarro's mature Impressionist period, when he was working alongside Cézanne and Gauguin in the region. It shows his characteristic broken brushwork applied to the rolling farmland of the Oise valley.
items.tags: Pontoise, Auvers, rural landscape, Oise valley, 1880s, road

items.title: The Louvre, Afternoon, Rainy Weather
items.description_narrative: One of Pissarro's late Paris cityscapes, painted from a hotel window overlooking the Louvre and the Seine during the final phase of his career when failing eyesight kept him working indoors. The rain-slicked pavement and diffused light are rendered through the same optical, broken-color technique he applied to his rural landscapes decades earlier.
items.tags: Paris, Louvre, cityscape, rain, late career, urban series
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: The Old Mill in Knokke
items.description_narrative: Painted during Pissarro's travels to the Belgian coastal town of Knokke, this work captures a windmill in the flat dune landscape typical of the region. It belongs to a small group of Belgian subjects he produced late in his career, applying his Impressionist eye to an unfamiliar northern landscape.
items.tags: Knokke, Belgium, windmill, coastal landscape, late career, 1890s

items.title: Afternoon Break, Girl and Young Peasant Woman Resting
items.description_narrative: A figure study of two peasant women pausing from field labor, typical of the rural genre scenes Pissarro increasingly favored in the early 1880s around Pontoise and Éragny. The painting reflects his growing interest in depicting agricultural labor with dignity rather than pure landscape.
items.tags: peasant women, rural labor, genre scene, figures, 1880s, rest

items.title: Rue de l'Hermitage, Pontoise
items.description_narrative: An early street view of L'Hermitage, the hillside quarter of Pontoise where Pissarro lived and worked repeatedly through the 1870s. Painted the year before his first prolonged stay there, it shows the tighter, more Realist brushwork of his pre-Impressionist years.
items.tags: Pontoise, L'Hermitage, street scene, early work, 1860s

items.title: Landscape, Ile-de-France
items.description_narrative: A rural view of the Ile-de-France countryside near Pontoise, painted at the height of Pissarro's collaboration with Cézanne, who worked alongside him in the region during the early 1870s. The loose, atmospheric handling is characteristic of his core Impressionist period.
items.tags: Ile-de-France, countryside, landscape, Pontoise, 1870s

items.title: The Pink House, Knokke
items.description_narrative: A view of a distinctively colored cottage in Knokke, Belgium, from Pissarro's travels along the Belgian coast in the 1890s. The bright facade set against open dunes let him explore the same color contrasts he pursued in his French rural scenes.
items.tags: Knokke, Belgium, cottage, coastal village, 1890s, architecture

items.title: The Orchard
items.description_narrative: A blossoming orchard scene from Pissarro's Louveciennes years, when he painted the fruit trees and kitchen gardens of the Seine valley village where he lived from 1869 to 1872. The subject reflects his lifelong preference for cultivated, working landscapes over wild scenery.
items.tags: orchard, Louveciennes, blossom, spring, garden, 1870s
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C.

items.title: In the Vegetable Garden
items.description_narrative: A kitchen-garden scene from Pissarro's Pontoise period, when depictions of peasants tending vegetable plots became a recurring theme in his work. The painting reflects his interest in everyday agricultural labor over more picturesque landscape subjects.
items.tags: vegetable garden, Pontoise, peasant labor, 1880s, kitchen garden

items.title: The Hermitage Gardens, Pontoise
items.description_narrative: A garden view from L'Hermitage, the hillside district of Pontoise where Pissarro settled for extended periods between 1866 and 1883. The painting dates from his earliest sustained residence there, before the Franco-Prussian War forced his temporary relocation to London.
items.tags: Pontoise, L'Hermitage, garden, landscape, 1860s

items.title: Ploughed Land
items.description_narrative: A study of freshly turned farmland near Pontoise, painted during Pissarro's most concentrated Impressionist decade in the region. The subject—bare furrowed earth under open sky—let him explore color and texture with minimal figuration.
items.tags: ploughed field, farmland, Pontoise, agriculture, 1870s

items.title: Young Peasant Girls Resting in the Fields near Pontoise
items.description_narrative: Two peasant girls pause from field work in the countryside outside Pontoise, a subject typical of the rural genre scenes Pissarro favored in the early 1880s. The painting is now in the collection of the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: peasant girls, rural labor, Pontoise, genre scene, 1880s
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: Houses at Bougival, Autumn
items.description_narrative: A view of the Seine-side village of Bougival, near Louveciennes where Pissarro was then living, painted shortly before the Franco-Prussian War disrupted his life and destroyed much of his earlier output. The autumnal palette reflects his growing sensitivity to seasonal light effects.
items.tags: Bougival, Seine valley, village, autumn, 1870s, houses

items.title: Peasant Woman
items.description_narrative: A single-figure study of a peasant woman, part of Pissarro's expanding interest in rural genre subjects around Pontoise and Éragny in the 1880s. The painting is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: peasant woman, figure study, rural life, 1880s
items.credit_line: 1. https://purl.org/nga/collection/artobject/46674 2. National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: Orchards at Louveciennes
items.description_narrative: A view of fruit orchards in Louveciennes, the Seine valley village where Pissarro lived from 1869 until the Franco-Prussian War forced his flight to London in late 1870. The painting is held by the Minneapolis Institute of Art.
items.tags: Louveciennes, orchard, Seine valley, landscape, 1870s

items.title: Peasant Woman Carrying Two Bundles of Hay
items.description_narrative: A figure study of a peasant woman carrying hay, reflecting Pissarro's mid-1880s turn toward monumental rural figures influenced in part by his exposure to Millet's example. The subject captures the physical labor of the agricultural cycle around Éragny and Pontoise.
items.tags: peasant woman, hay, rural labor, figure study, 1880s
items.credit_line: Dallas Museum of Art, online collection

items.title: Apple Harvest, Éragny
items.description_narrative: A scene of apple picking at Éragny-sur-Epte, the Normandy village where Pissarro settled in 1884 and remained for the rest of his life. The subject reflects the working orchards and farmland surrounding his final home, a recurring theme in his 1880s and 1890s output.
items.tags: Eragny, apple harvest, orchard, rural labor, 1880s
items.credit_line: The Dallas Museum of Art, object page

items.title: Chestnut Grove, Louveciennes
items.description_narrative: A wooded view near Louveciennes, painted after Pissarro returned to France from his wartime exile in London and resettled briefly in the Seine valley before moving to Pontoise. The stand of chestnut trees is a recurring motif in his early-1870s landscapes of the area.
items.tags: Louveciennes, chestnut trees, woodland, landscape, 1870s
items.credit_line: Google Art Project works from the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art

items.title: Route d'Ennery
items.description_narrative: A rural road near Pontoise, painted during the period Pissarro exhibited in the first Impressionist exhibition of 1874. The canvas is held by the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
items.tags: Pontoise, road, rural landscape, Musee d'Orsay, 1870s

items.title: Lordship Lane Station, Dulwich
items.description_narrative: Painted during Pissarro's wartime exile in London, this view of a suburban railway station in Dulwich is one of the earliest paintings anywhere to depict a train and station as a primary subject. It reflects his brief but productive period working alongside Monet in England during the Franco-Prussian War.
items.tags: London, Dulwich, railway station, England, 1871, exile period
items.credit_line: 2. Courtauld Gallery1. Transferred from en.wikipedia to Commons. Transfer was stated to be made by User:oxyman. Original uploader was Brendanconway at en.wikipedia 2005-02-07 (original upload date)

items.title: The Big Walnut Tree, Autumn Morning, Éragny
items.description_narrative: A view of a large walnut tree near Pissarro's house at Éragny-sur-Epte, painted in the misty morning light he favored in his later landscape work. The canvas is held by the Pushkin Museum, Moscow.
items.tags: Eragny, walnut tree, autumn, morning light, 1890s

items.title: Banks of the Seine at Port-Marly
items.description_narrative: Painted shortly after Pissarro's return from London following the Franco-Prussian War, this riverside view of Port-Marly reflects his renewed engagement with the Seine valley landscapes near his home. The subject and handling connect it to the plein-air river scenes he and Monet had explored together in exile.
items.tags: Port-Marly, Seine river, riverside, landscape, 1870s
items.credit_line: Google Art Project works from the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art

items.title: The Hay Harvest, Éragny
items.description_narrative: A scene of hay gathering near Éragny-sur-Epte, painted during the mid-1880s when Pissarro briefly adopted the pointillist technique of his younger colleagues Seurat and Signac. The subject of collective farm labor recurs throughout his Éragny-period work.
items.tags: Eragny, hay harvest, rural labor, farmland, 1880s

items.title: View from Louveciennes
items.description_narrative: A panoramic landscape from the hillside above Louveciennes, painted during Pissarro's residence there just before the Franco-Prussian War. The canvas is held by the National Gallery, London.
items.tags: Louveciennes, panoramic view, Seine valley, landscape, 1870s
items.credit_line: 2. National Gallery, London - online catalogue. 1. The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN: 3936122202.

items.title: Hoar-Frost, Peasant Girl Making a Fire
items.description_narrative: A winter genre scene showing a peasant girl tending a fire under frost-covered trees, painted during Pissarro's mid-1880s experimentation with pointillist technique. The subject combines his interest in seasonal atmospheric effects with rural figure work.
items.tags: hoarfrost, winter, peasant girl, fire, rural genre, 1880s

items.title: Julie Pissarro in the Garden
items.description_narrative: A domestic portrait of the artist's wife, Julie Vellay, in the garden of their home, painted during their years at Pontoise. Julie appears in several of Pissarro's paintings of this period, reflecting the intimate, family-centered subjects he pursued alongside his landscape work.
items.tags: Julie Pissarro, wife, garden, domestic scene, portrait, 1870s

items.title: Portrait of a Boy
items.description_narrative: An early portrait dating from Pissarro's youth in the Caribbean and Venezuela, before he settled permanently in France in 1855 to pursue painting seriously. Works from this formative period are rare, predating his mature engagement with landscape and Impressionism.
items.tags: early work, portrait, Caribbean, Venezuela, pre-Impressionist

items.title: Landscape at Saint-Charles, near Gisors, Sunset
items.description_narrative: A sunset landscape near Gisors, north of Pontoise, painted while Pissarro was working in the broken, dotted brushwork of his Neo-Impressionist phase. The canvas is held by the Clark Art Institute.
items.tags: Gisors, sunset, landscape, Neo-Impressionism, 1880s

items.title: June Morning at Pontoise
items.description_narrative: A morning landscape near Pontoise from the height of Pissarro's collaboration with Cézanne, who worked alongside him in the town through the early 1870s. The soft early light reflects his growing interest in capturing specific times of day.
items.tags: Pontoise, morning, June, landscape, 1870s

items.title: A Cowherd at Valhermeil, Auvers-sur-Oise
items.description_narrative: A pastoral scene set on the hillside at Valhermeil, near Auvers-sur-Oise, painted while Pissarro was based in nearby Pontoise. The canvas is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
items.tags: Auvers-sur-Oise, cowherd, pastoral, hillside, 1870s

items.title: Landscape
items.description_narrative: An early landscape predating Pissarro's mature Impressionist style, painted while he was still working under the influence of the Barbizon School and Corot. It reflects his formative years before settling into the broken-brushwork technique he developed in the 1870s.
items.tags: early work, landscape, Barbizon influence, 1860s

items.title: The Little Country Maid
items.description_narrative: A single-figure genre study of a young servant girl, painted during Pissarro's prolific early-1880s period of rural figure subjects around Pontoise and Osny. It reflects his shift toward more intimate, close-up figure compositions in this decade.
items.tags: peasant girl, genre scene, figure study, 1880s

items.title: The Pork Butcher
items.description_narrative: A market genre scene depicting a butcher at her stall, one of several tradeswoman subjects Pissarro painted in the early 1880s as he expanded beyond landscape into scenes of commerce and daily labor. The composition reflects his interest in ordinary working women as serious painterly subjects.
items.tags: market scene, butcher, tradeswoman, genre painting, 1880s

items.title: Two Women Chatting by the Sea, St. Thomas
items.description_narrative: Painted on the Caribbean island of St. Thomas, where Pissarro was born and spent his early life before permanently relocating to France, this coastal scene dates from a brief return visit in the mid-1850s. The canvas is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: St. Thomas, Caribbean, coastal scene, early work, 1850s
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C. – The Collection – Two Women Chatting by the Sea, St. Thomas

items.title: Two Young Peasant Women
items.description_narrative: A double figure study of peasant women, painted during Pissarro's later Éragny years when rural labor and peasant life remained his central subject alongside landscape. The canvas is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
items.tags: peasant women, figure study, rural life, 1890s

items.title: Portrait of Félix in a Skirt
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Pissarro's son Félix as a young child, dressed in the skirted garments customary for small boys in the period. Family members, especially his children, appear frequently throughout Pissarro's portrait work.
items.tags: Felix Pissarro, family portrait, child, 1880s

items.title: In the Garden of Les Mathurins, Pontoise
items.description_narrative: A garden scene set at Les Mathurins, a property in Pontoise, painted at the height of Pissarro's core Impressionist period there. The subject reflects his continuing preference for cultivated, domestic landscapes over wilder scenery.
items.tags: Pontoise, garden, Les Mathurins, landscape, 1870s
items.credit_line: [1], Picture prepared for Wikipedia by Adrian Pingstone in April 2003.

items.title: The Poultry Market, Pontoise
items.description_narrative: A bustling market scene set in Pontoise, one of several market and street subjects Pissarro painted in the early 1880s that shifted his focus toward town life and commerce alongside his rural landscapes.
items.tags: Pontoise, market scene, poultry, town life, 1880s

items.title: Two Women Kneeling at the Wash-House
items.description_narrative: A genre scene of laundresses at work, a subject Pissarro returned to periodically throughout his career as an emblem of everyday rural and small-town labor. The wash-house was a common gathering place for women in provincial French communities of the period.
items.tags: washerwomen, laundry, genre scene, rural life

items.title: The Louvre Under Snow
items.description_narrative: A snow-covered view of the Louvre painted from Pissarro's Paris apartment window near the end of his life, when eye trouble confined much of his work to views from indoors. It belongs to his late series of Paris cityscapes exploring weather and seasonal light over the same urban vista.
items.tags: Paris, Louvre, snow, cityscape, late career, 1900s

items.title: Still Life
items.description_narrative: A rare still life within Pissarro's largely landscape- and figure-focused body of work, reflecting an academic exercise more typical of his early training than his mature Impressionist practice.
items.tags: still life, early work, 1860s

items.title: The Village of Knokke
items.description_narrative: A view of the village of Knokke on the Belgian coast, from Pissarro's travels there in the mid-1890s. It belongs to a small group of Belgian subjects distinct from his more extensive French landscape output.
items.tags: Knokke, Belgium, village, coastal landscape, 1890s

items.title: Vegetable Garden
items.description_narrative: A kitchen-garden landscape from Pissarro's Pontoise years, when depictions of cultivated plots and market gardens were a recurring subject. The painting reflects his consistent preference for working, productive land over untouched scenery.
items.tags: vegetable garden, Pontoise, cultivated land, 1870s
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture: Home page – Image

items.title: Peasants' Houses, Éragny
items.description_narrative: A view of rural cottages at Éragny-sur-Epte, the Normandy village that became Pissarro's permanent home from 1884 onward. The modest houses reflect his continued focus on the working countryside rather than picturesque or grand architecture.
items.tags: Eragny, peasant houses, village, rural architecture, 1880s
items.credit_line: QgGHxgs5iZgNnA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Seine at Bougival
items.description_narrative: A riverside view of Bougival on the Seine, painted shortly after Pissarro's return to France from London following the Franco-Prussian War. It reflects his renewed engagement with the river landscapes of the Seine valley near Louveciennes.
items.tags: Bougival, Seine river, landscape, 1870s
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture: Home page – QQHISYDhTvHr4Q Image

items.title: Poultry Market at Gisors
items.description_narrative: A market scene set in the town of Gisors, north of Pontoise, painted during Pissarro's mid-1880s turn toward market and town subjects alongside his rural landscapes and his brief experimentation with pointillist technique.
items.tags: Gisors, market scene, poultry, town life, 1880s
items.credit_line: -QFl_G1j8hU_fw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Sunlight on the Road, Pontoise
items.description_narrative: A road landscape near Pontoise exploring the effect of direct sunlight on a dirt track, painted during the height of Pissarro's core Impressionist period working alongside Cézanne in the town.
